title: "Make It Warmer" Is Not a Prompt. So I Turned It Into Taps | vitalii.no
description:
How a tap-based Telegram menu let non-technical moderators steer AI image generation, cutting 2 hours of trial and error to 15 minutes.

AI-generated article images kept missing the mark, and the feedback that came back was unusable as a prompt. "More corporate." "Warmer colors." Everyone knew what they wanted; nobody could write it in the form an image model reads. So the loop became regenerate, look, regenerate again — more than 2 hours of guessing per article.

The Creative Builder is a Telegram bot interface built on the Telegram Bot API with Supabase holding the session state. Inline keyboard callbacks drive everything: cb_hub_${uuid} opens 7 creative categories, each with 6 options, 42 no-code elements in total. Tapping a category then an option stores the choice against the session. When cb_gen fires, every tap is compiled into one real prompt and sent to Azure OpenAI, which draws the image. The moderator never types a word.

Iteration time per article dropped from 2 hours of trial and error to 15 minutes, an 87 percent reduction, and creative direction moved to the people who actually have an opinion about it, without any prompt engineering.
